conviction_note: The bear case here is maximally priced (largest downside skew in the day's universe at +18.59, -23.1% in 20 days, consensus EPS cut 47% to $0.42 in a month, ~53% of float short) while a specific, quantifiable positive is not in any preview: RH's CFO said on 11 Jun that IEEPA tariff refunds had 'started coming' and that FY26 FCF guidance of $300-400m assumes none, and Williams-Sonoma — same industry, quarter ended 2 Aug 2026 versus RH's 1 Aug 2026 — collected $200.2m of refund and booked $167.8m into COGS in exactly that window; net of an almost-certain FY guide cut that is already the consensus, the distribution skews modestly up.

findings.finding: RH's FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance of $300-400m explicitly assumes zero further IEEPA tariff refunds (CFO Jack Preston, 11 Jun 2026: 'the refund started coming, but... they have been kind of paused'), yet the refund machinery ran hard through exactly RH's fiscal Q2 — the closest comparable, Williams-Sonoma, collected $200.2m against a $197.8m claim and recognised $167.8m as a reduction in cost of goods sold plus $6.3m of interest income in the quarter ended 2 August 2026, one day after RH's own quarter end.
findings.why_not_priced: Scaled on revenue, WSM's $197.8m claim implies roughly $60-90m for RH — against a $2.63bn market cap, a $53.8m cash balance, $30m already drawn on the ABL and a consensus EPS of $0.42 on 18.9m shares, i.e. potentially several dollars of GAAP EPS and more than the entire cash balance in one line. If the market had priced it you would see (a) RH's own preview coverage naming it — the 9 Sep 2026 Parameter preview does not mention tariff refunds, IEEPA or a customs receivable once, attributing the whole decline to 380bp of Paris/Milan start-up costs and housing; (b) RH bid, not down another 3%, in the ten sessions after WSM disclosed its refund on 26 Aug; and (c) call skew, not a +18.59 vol-point put skew and a 1.49 put/call OI ratio, on the single most levered balance sheet in the group (net debt $2.37bn, 4.3x TTM EBITDA) where a cash windfall is worth most. It is off-model because it is not an EPS-line item anyone forecasts: it is a customs receivable, excluded by management from its own guidance.
findings.independence: Williams-Sonoma's Q2 FY2026 release, a different company and a different document, is the corroborating datapoint and quantifies the mechanism: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WSM/williams-sonoma-inc-announces-strong-second-quarter-2026-j5qlnab2ts07.html (2026-08-26). The same release also reports comp gains across WSM's portfolio and a raised annual outlook for the identical quarter, an independent read that RH's Q2 end-demand was not the disaster the skew implies — I am not filing that separately because it rests on the same WSM document as the refund evidence.

findings.finding: RH's own H2 revenue bridge to the ~12% second-half growth its FY guide requires is 4.5pp backlog + 2.5pp new stores + 5.0pp RH Estates — and RH has issued no press release announcing the opening of either standalone RH Estates gallery (Greenwich CT, San Francisco Design District), despite pressing out a release for every other opening including RH Milan (15 May) and RH London Mayfair (6 Jul); its last release before the print is dated 3 September 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The street prices 'RH will cut the FY guide' generically — that is why EPS consensus fell from $0.79 to $0.42 in a month. What is not priced is the specific mechanism: 5 of the 12 H2 points come from a concept launched 1 July 2026 that is still only an assortment inside existing Design Galleries, and the absence of an opening release is checkable against RH's own demonstrated cadence of announcing every gallery. If this were focused on, previews would be interrogating the Estates ramp rather than the 380bp start-up drag. Sized small because the guide cut itself is consensus and therefore mostly in the price.
findings.independence: RH's own press-release index, showing the gap, is a different source: https://ir.rh.com/news-events/press-releases (list current to 2026-09-03). The 1 Jul 2026 RH Estates launch release names Greenwich and West Hollywood standalone stores with no opening dates attached: https://ir.rh.com/news-events/detail/284/rh-announces-the-unveiling-of-rh-estates-making-the-work-of-the-worlds-most-legendary-designers-and-ateliers-accessible-to-consumers-for-the-first-time

findings.finding: Gary Friedman, who owns 23.88% of RH, sold 125,000 shares over 6-8 July 2026 and RH put out a press release saying the proceeds went to 'the repayment of balances under personal line of credit borrowings' — i.e. the CEO is personally levered against RH stock, and the stock has fallen a further ~27% since (from roughly $190 in early July to $138.57).
findings.why_not_priced: The sale itself was covered in July, but the stated *reason* — personal credit-line repayment — was not, and it converts a routine insider sale into a standing forced-supply risk on a stock with only 18.9m shares outstanding. If the market had priced a Friedman margin overhang you would see it named in previews and in the borrow; no 2026 preview I found mentions it, and RH's own press release frames it as a positive ('remains a buyer of RH shares'). Sized small: it is an overhang, not a print-day catalyst.
findings.independence: none — the Form 144s filed 6, 7, 8 and 10 July 2026 on EDGAR are the same transaction, not independent confirmation.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the -23% 20-day drawdown: no RH 8-K, press release or Form 4/144 exists between 23 July and 3 September 2026 (EDGAR submissions API, RH IR index), so the Aug 18 $171 to Aug 24 $143 slide had no company-specific trigger I could identify

Any RH-specific disclosure of the size of its IEEPA refund claim — a $69m figure surfaced in an AI-generated search summary but I could not source it to any dated document and have therefore not used it
Whether the RH Estates Greenwich Ave gallery has physically opened — local Greenwich reporting still says 'spring/summer 2026' with no confirmed opening, but nothing definitive
Any closed Aspen property sale between the 11 June call and the print that would evidence the $200-250m/yr asset-monetisation target
Covenant, going-concern or refinancing language in the Q1 10-Q — none found; term loans are covenant-lite as far as the filing shows
Any 13D/A or 13G/A indicating a large-holder liquidation in August (the 14 Aug 13G/A is Citadel Securities, a market maker)
Recent hiring-page, app-store or support-forum signal on RH — rh.com returns 403 to automated fetches
baseline_tension: It cuts hard against the baseline: the +18.59 skew, the 1.49 put/call OI ratio and the -23.1% run-up all say downside, and my largest finding is a positive one that argues precisely that the downside is what has been paid for while an off-guidance, off-consensus cash item sitting in the quarter that just closed has not.
